text:
incident-bot: ALERT: streaming-gateway elevated 5xx rate + frequent client disconnects in us-west-2 since 23:07 UTC. error pattern: chunked_trailer_corrupt / early_eof / client_cancel spikes. Thresholds breached: 5xx > 3x baseline, timeouts > 2x. P50 latency OK, P95 increasing. Paging route fallback firing for some sessions. Paging: 12% of streams falling back to paged responses.

Jordan (oncall): Ack, I'm on it. Starting triage. @Carla S. can you pull gateway logs for 23:00-23:15? I want connection reset patterns and any deploys.

Carla S.: pulling logs now. quick grep shows a rise in `HTTP/1.1 502` and `HTTP/1.1 524` with chunked-transfer-encoding warnings. sample tail: ```
[23:08:12] gateway://gw-17 - peer reset during transfer: EOF while reading chunked body
[23:08:13] gateway://gw-03 - upstream 502 bad gateway (connection reset)
[23:09:01] gw-17 - client-cancel received before trailer (len=0)
```

Alice M.: noticed increased kernel-level RSTs on gw-17 around 23:07. netstat shows many connections in TIME_WAIT then immediate new attempts. suspicion: TCP backlog pressure + keepalive mismatch with client libs.

Jordan (oncall): Any recent infra changes? autoscaler? keepalive config? deploys?

Ben K.: No infra deploys in last hour. There was a small streaming-runtime tweak at 22:50 that adjusted chunk flushing intervals (PR #556). It was canary rolled to 5% in us-west and we saw slight CPU bump on gw-17. Rolling back now to be safe.

deploy-bot: Rollback started: rolling back streaming-runtime PR #556 from gw-17 and gw-03 canaries. ETA ~3m. :construction:

Carla S.: while rollback runs, attaching a short query of errors by route: ```
route streaming.chat: 5xx spike 23:07-23:12 (peak 6.4%)
route streaming.embeddings: 5xx spike 23:08-23:11 (peak 4.8%)
route paged.fanout: increased traffic due to fallback, errors mostly downstream timeouts
```

Jordan (oncall): Customer impact? any 1:1 reports?

Customer Ops: We have two customers reporting aborted streams and truncated outputs (customer-A and customer-B). Both are on us-west. Customer-A saw 20% of requests drop to truncated payloads; Customer-B saw client cancel rate spike from 0.2% -> 7%. POV: moderate customer impact for a subset of heavy streaming consumers.

Kevin L.: running a quick grafana query. Kernel RSTs correlate with an increase in conn-syn retries when gw-17 CPU > 70%. Looks like backlog queue is hitting limits then upstream closes.

Jordan (oncall): Mitigations I'm ordering now: 1) complete rollback of PR #556 (in progress). 2) temporarily increase accept backlog and tcp_keepalive_time on gw nodes. 3) enable per-route streaming-paged fallback for affected customers only. 4) short-term routing to healthy region (us-east-1) for high-risk tenants. 5) enable verbose streaming debug on gw-17 for 10m.

Carla S.: rollback finished on gw-17 and gw-03. Metrics: 5xx started trending down within 90s on gw-03, gw-17 slower to recover.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete for PR #556. Canary removed. :white_check_mark:

Ben K.: I pushed a temporary kube patch to increase `tcp-max-backlog` and bumped node `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time` from 600 -> 1200 on gw-17/03. Applied via k8s daemonset. Watch for side effects.

Alice M.: after backlog bump, connection resets fell by ~40% over the next 2m. Streaming continuity improved for many sessions. Still seeing some client-cancel spikes — likely clients timing out.

Jordan (oncall): Rolling targeted routing now: moving customer-A traffic to us-east-1 for immediate relief. Ben, can you confirm the route rule?

Ben K.: done. customer-A is now routed to us-east-1 via policy:tenant-route/customer-A -> us-east-1-gw-pool. Confirming health checks green.

Customer Ops: customer-A reports streams resumed, fewer truncations. They still saw 1 failed session in last 5m.

Carla S.: verbose debug logs show repeated message: `chunked: trailer missing - upstream closed mid-chunk`. Suspect either a library-level premature close or a GC pause in the runtime that dropped the connection while KV cache flush in progress.

Jordan (oncall): Good catch. Carla, can you collect a flame/gc profile from the runtime for the canary nodes (if any active) and grep for GC pauses > 100ms in 22:45-23:15 window?

Carla S.: starting profiling. quick grep shows a couple GC pauses ~140-180ms on gw-17 at 22:51 (from earlier canary) but nothing at 23:07. So GC may have contributed earlier during canary but current 23:07 spike aligns more with backlog pressure.

Alice M.: Recommendation: keep rollback in place for 1h, keep backlog/keepalive changes for 30m and monitor. Also add a temporary client-side retry header to instruct SDKs to increase streaming read timeouts by 2x for affected tenants.

Jordan (oncall): Agreed. I'll escalate to oncall rotation that next up is Ben K. — handing off active incident. Ben, you own the post-mitigation watch and next 1h of monitoring. If error rate goes above 1.5x baseline again, page SRE lead.

Ben K.: Taking over. I'll keep watch and update every 15m. Current state: 5xx back down to 1.1x baseline, timeouts still 1.4x. Rolling watch enabled.

Carla S.: creating a ticket for root cause investigation: `INC-4105-streaming-heartbeat-drop` with notes: possible combo of small canary change + kernel backlog starvation + client timeout sensitivity. Will attach debug logs and flame profiles.

incident-bot: Pager log entry: incident 4105009999 assigned to Ben K.; severity: SEV2; summary: streaming gateway intermittent disconnects and chunked encoding failures in us-west-2; mitigations: rollback, backlog bump, targeted routing.

Jordan (oncall): Leaving detailed TODOs in the ticket: - full postmortem if incident reoccurs - evaluate streaming-runtime flush behavior under load - add automated detector for chunked-trailer-missing alerts - consider gradual canary policy changes (lower CPU delta threshold).

Ben K.: I'll coordinate with Customer Ops to send a short status update to affected customers in 30m. For now, marking the incident as "mitigated" but not resolved. I'll ping here for closure after the watch window. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Customer Ops: Thanks — we'll prepare the customer message draft and hold for Ben's go-ahead.

Jordan (oncall): Good job team. Logging out of active triage, handoff complete.

Ben K.: 15m check-in: metrics stable, no new region-wide spikes. continuing watch.

Carla S.: uploaded logs + debug bundle to the ticket: s3://redwood-incident/4105/debug-bundle.tar.gz

Ben K.: 45m check-in: still stable. scheduling follow-up RCA meeting for tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Will invite Alice, Carla, Jordan, and runtime owners.

incident-bot: Incident 4105009999 status updated to MITIGATED by Ben K.

Ben K.: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see regression. :wave:
